why: parent.ts holds five type errors under strict mode: two possibly absent receivers (TS18048), an implicit-any parameter, a local written any, and a cast the compiler rejects (TS2352). candidate.ts is exactly what lean convert makes of it: the strict family writes the proposed type at the two declarations, and lists the two absent reads (a narrowing a person writes: `x!` is refused as non-null-assertion and `?.` changes the absent case) and the cast (a migration). Each annotation is erased from the emitted JavaScript, so the converter gives each changed unit the verdict PASS-erased (the emit hashes under both settings and the unit's self-proof in its certificate). Lane A cannot prove the annotations against parent.ts: scaled's parameter goes from any to number (ASK:interface) and label reads a boxed any against a number (unproved, PASS-bounded); the unconverted units stay outside the subset (PASS-bounded). Once annotated, scaled and label are inside the subset and proved (candidate against itself). wrong.ts is the `?.` rewrite at an absent read, `u.name?.length ?? 0`: it returns 0 where the parent throws, and lane B witnesses it. Since a strict-mode error's value is read at Any (2026-10-30, design/strict-fixer.md), nameLength and cityOf in candidate.ts are proved, not only bounded.
